DE-C2-01-001.notes: im Grunde (basically) keeps the old dative -e, which modern German has otherwise dropped. Such frozen forms survive in set phrases: im Laufe, zu Hause.

DE-C2-01-002.notes: auf dem Lande keeps the old dative -e and sounds old-fashioned; auf dem Land is the modern form. auf dem Land itself means 'in the country(side)'.

DE-C2-01-003.notes: ward is the old past of werden, now only biblical or poetic: Und es ward Licht (Genesis). The modern form is wurde.

DE-C2-01-004.notes: wes is the old genitive of wer (= wessen). The proverb keeps elided forms (ess', sing') for rhythm. des is the matching old demonstrative: whose bread I eat, his song I sing.

DE-C2-01-005.notes: jener (that) contrasts with dieser in written style and declines like it: jenes Haus. In speech, der da or das andere is used.
DE-C2-01-005.tr: It's not this house I'd like to buy, but that one.

DE-C2-01-006.notes: welch ein …! (what a…!) is a literary exclamation with uninflected welch. Everyday speech uses Was für ein…!

DE-C2-02-001.notes: eines Tages (one day) is an adverbial genitive. The time phrase takes first position, so the verb wirst follows.

DE-C2-02-002.notes: meines Wissens (as far as I know) is a fixed genitive phrase, written and formal. Speech prefers soweit ich weiß.

DE-C2-02-003.notes: letzten Endes (ultimately) is a genitive phrase with adjective -en. letztendlich is a common one-word synonym.

DE-C2-02-004.notes: allen Ernstes (in all seriousness) is a fixed genitive and often implies the speaker's disbelief. It usually follows the verb.

DE-C2-02-005.notes: schweren Herzens (with a heavy heart) is a fixed genitive of manner. Herz takes -ens in the genitive.

DE-C2-02-006.notes: unverrichteter Dinge (without achieving anything) is a genitive plural phrase. It's formal and slightly ironic.

DE-C2-03-001.notes: meinetwegen literally means 'because of me' but is mostly used as 'fine by me, I don't mind'. The -et- links the pronoun to -wegen.

DE-C2-03-002.notes: deinetwegen = because of you. The pattern gives seinetwegen, ihretwegen, unsertwegen. It's written as one word.

DE-C2-03-003.notes: um … willen (for the sake of) wraps a genitive: um Himmels willen. Um Gottes willen is the stronger variant.

DE-C2-03-004.notes: um des lieben Friedens willen = for the sake of peace and quiet. The genitive sits between um and willen.

DE-C2-03-005.notes: statt meiner uses the genitive pronoun meiner, which is formal. Colloquial German says statt mir. Likewise statt seiner, statt ihrer.

DE-C2-04-001.notes: möge (Konjunktiv I of mögen) expresses a formal wish: Man möge mir verzeihen. Möge er in Frieden ruhen is a common formula.

DE-C2-04-002.notes: An indirect command uses Konjunktiv I of sollen: Er sagte, ich solle warten. In speech, ich soll or ich sollte.

DE-C2-04-003.notes: Indirect questions can take Konjunktiv I: ob er komme. Speech normally uses the indicative: ob er kommt.

DE-C2-04-004.notes: müssen gives sie müsse in Konjunktiv I, without the umlaut change of the indicative singular (muss).

DE-C2-05-001.notes: so + adjective + auch means 'however…': So schwer es auch ist. The main clause usually keeps normal word order (wir geben…).

DE-C2-05-002.notes: was auch immer = whatever. auch immer can also follow the verb: Was immer passiert… The main clause keeps verb-second order.

DE-C2-05-003.notes: wer auch immer = whoever. The main clause refers back with er or der. In speech, wer immer or just wer is also used.

DE-C2-05-004.notes: Mag es noch so regnen = however much it may rain. mögen here is concessive, not 'like'. The main clause keeps normal order: wir gehen.

DE-C2-06-001.notes: binnen (within) is legal and official; it takes the dative (binnen 14 Tagen) or the genitive. In everyday German, innerhalb von is used.

DE-C2-06-002.notes: unbeschadet + genitive = without prejudice to. It's a fixed legal formula. It's often placed at the start of the sentence.

DE-C2-06-003.notes: vorbehaltlich + genitive = subject to. The noun is der Vorbehalt (reservation). unter Vorbehalt means 'with reservations'.

DE-C2-06-004.notes: sein + zu in legal texts means 'must be done': sind vorzulegen. vorlegen is separable, so zu goes in the middle.

DE-C2-06-005.notes: haben + zu in contracts imposes an obligation: Der Mieter hat … zu tragen (shall bear). English legal texts use 'shall' in the same way.

DE-C2-06-006.notes: sofern nicht anders vereinbart = unless otherwise agreed. The auxiliary ist is dropped, as often in legal shorthand.

DE-C2-07-001.notes: Atlas has the learned plural Atlanten; Atlasse is also accepted. Atlas is also the name of the Titan and of the mountains.

DE-C2-07-002.notes: Kaktus has the learned plural Kakteen; Kaktusse is colloquial. The singular Kaktus is masculine, and the noun counts as a Latin loan.

DE-C2-07-003.notes: Visum has the Latin plural Visa (or Visen). The same -um → -a pattern gives Praktikum → Praktika. The singular is das Visum.

DE-C2-07-004.notes: Komma has the plural Kommata (learned) or Kommas (everyday). Both are correct. The singular is das Komma.

DE-C2-07-005.notes: Museum has the plural Museen: -um is replaced by -en. Likewise Zentrum → Zentren, Studium → Studien.

DE-C2-07-006.notes: Praktikum has the plural Praktika. ein Praktikum machen = do an internship. Its plural Praktika is the only form in use.

DE-C2-08-001.notes: Names take -s in the genitive and can follow the noun in formal style: die Werke Goethes. Goethes Werke is equally correct.

DE-C2-08-002.notes: Names ending in -s, -ß, -x or -z take only an apostrophe in the genitive: Hans' Schwester. In speech von is used.
DE-C2-08-002.text: {{c1::Hans'::Hans · genitive (name ending in -s)}} Schwester wohnt in Köln.
DE-C2-08-002.flag: dup: replaced Das ist Hans' Auto (near-identical to A2-12-001 Das ist Annas Auto)

DE-C2-08-003.notes: With an article and a title, only the article and the title change: das Büro des Herrn Müller. The name itself stays.

DE-C2-08-004.notes: Without an article, the name takes the -s: Herrn Müllers Vortrag. Herr still takes its n-noun -n. Both versions are correct; the second is more modern.
DE-C2-08-004.text: {{c1::Herrn::Herr · genitive (no article; … Müllers)}} Müllers Vortrag hat allen gefallen.
DE-C2-08-004.flag: dup: replaced Herrn Müllers Büro ist im zweiten Stock (same sentence as C2-08-003)

DE-C2-09-001.notes: Fronting the participle puts contrastive stress on it: Gesehen habe ich ihn nicht (but heard him). The verb stays second.

DE-C2-09-002.notes: Geschlafen hat er kaum: the fronted participle is the topic. English needs a cleft: as for sleep… The verb hat stays second.
DE-C2-09-002.tr: As for sleep, he hardly got any.

DE-C2-09-003.notes: An infinitive can be fronted too: Helfen kann ich dir nicht. The modal stays in second place. The subject ich comes after the modal.

DE-C2-10-001.notes: sterben has the old Konjunktiv II stürbe, with ü. Modern German uses würde sterben. The main clause uses erbte, an ambiguous form for Konjunktiv II.

DE-C2-10-002.notes: helfen has the literary Konjunktiv II hülfe (also hälfe). In speech: würde helfen. Both forms sound archaic today.

DE-C2-10-003.notes: empfehlen has the literary Konjunktiv II empföhle (also empfähle). Today: würde empfehlen. Ich würde Ihnen … empfehlen is the everyday form.
